sentence: This project produces swine models that stand in for human conditions and helps test tools for editing genes.
This project provides bioinformatic and statistical support to vision researchers running clinical, genomic and laboratory studies.
This project supports research on the causes, diagnosis and treatment of liver diseases and related disorders of the digestive system.
This project builds simulation approaches and population genetic models to understand the expected outcomes of rapid evolutionary processes such as CRISPR gene drives.
This project builds disease models in a small nematode worm to study how neurotoxic disease spreads from the gut to the brain in Parkinson's disease.
This project uses single-cell sequencing of human eye tissues, including the optic nerve head and retina, to find genes and cell types that affect glaucoma.
This project tests whether a drug called verteporfin can treat glioblastoma, using organoid models, animal models and human patient specimens.
This project provides database and statistical support for a study of the aging brain, including tools to track cognitive change.
This project tests whether methylation profiling of DNA circulating in the blood can diagnose brain tumors and track treatment response and recurrence.
This project studies how invasive trophoblast cells and uterine cells build the uterine-placental interface that pregnancy depends on.
This project builds tools to target and change feedback pathways in the primate brain to study their role in visual perception and motor planning.
This project studies the structure of hepatitis B virus particles made in human hepatoma cells.
This project builds brain growth chart models from clinically acquired brain scans to find brain profiles linked to high genetic risk for neurodevelopmental disorders.
This project studies how a single RNA nucleotide modification guides the differentiation of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells.
This project studies whether losing acetate-producing gut bacteria drives chronic neurodegeneration and microglial activation after traumatic brain injury.
This project uses a mouse model to study how alcohol exposure in the third trimester causes learning and memory deficits.
This project supports research on how nutrition and metabolism affect health and chronic diseases such as diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular disorders.
This project supports the creation, breeding and maintenance of genetically engineered mouse models of cancer.
This project provides biostatistics and bioinformatics support for designing and analyzing experiments and studies on cancer.
This project studies how lung cancer spreads to other organs and how common mutations stimulate lung cancer growth.
